drivingQuestion: From where do we know that paternal brothers inherit and bequeath to each other?
outcomeNote: Rabba's gezera shava supplies the source (challenged in the next unit).

segments.he: וְהָאַחִין מִן הָאָב נוֹחֲלִין וּמַנְחִילִין וְכוּ׳. מְנָלַן? אָמַר רַבָּה: אַתְיָא ״אַחְוָה״–״אַחְוָה״ מִבְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב; מַה לְהַלָּן, מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם; אַף כָּאן, מִן הָאָב וְלֹא מִן הָאֵם.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And paternal brothers inherit» from one another «and bequeath» to each other. «From where do we» derive this halakha? «Rabba said:» It «is derived from» a verbal analogy between the word: «Brothers,» stated with regard to inheritance, and the word: «Brothers,» found in the verses concerning «Jacob’s sons.» When Jacob’s sons speak to Joseph, they state: “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan” (Genesis 42:13), and in the passage discussing inheritance the verse states: “And if he has no brothers, then you shall give his inheritance to his father’s brothers” (Numbers 27:10). «Just as there,» in the verse concerning Jacob’s sons, the word brothers is referring to «paternal» brothers «and not maternal» brothers, as the twelve of them shared only the same father, «so too here,» where this term is used with regard to inheritance, the verse is referring to «paternal» brothers «and not maternal» brothers.
